title: Network-isolation egress fails with HIER_NONE after the host accepts Tailscale routes
symptoms: Every CONNECT to an allowlisted API host fails with 503 TCP_TUNNEL:HIER_NONE and an empty server field (-:-) in network-isolation (topology) mode
The same workflow succeeds in host-access mode, or in isolation mode when no Tailscale step runs
Agent retries report 503 Service Unavailable from the model endpoint while the allowlist already contains the host
conditions: AWF runs with network isolation, so Squid egresses through the dual-homed awf-ext bridge and the host routing tables
A Tailscale step runs on the runner and accepts advertised subnet routes (--accept-routes), which add policy routes in table 52 consulted before the main table
An accepted subnet may capture Squid's traffic to a resolver or API destination via the tailnet interface
A policy denial (TCP_DENIED / 403) or an awf-net subnet collision (NET-006) is a different cause and does not match
The route-capture mechanism comes from one reporter's analysis; only the routing-acceptance change below was validated
rootCause: In network-isolation mode AWF delegates egress to the host network stack and does not install or pin host policy routes. A Tailscale step that accepts advertised subnet routes inserts policy-routing entries ahead of the main table; the reporter suspected an accepted subnet captured Squid's outbound connections or name lookups into the tailnet interface. The earlier theory that a non-portable resolver such as 168.63.129.16 was the sole cause was not sufficient: the resolver-filtering change was merged and later reverted, and the failure persisted until route acceptance was disabled. The mechanism rests on one reporter's investigation.

probe.command: ip rule show; ip route show table main; ip route show table 52
probe.expect: Compare the policy rules and table 52 with the main routes; this is preliminary evidence, not proof that Squid's traffic is captured or unaffected. For each affected resolver and API destination IP, perform a host-side `ip route get <destination-ip> from <squid-awf-ext-ip> iif <awf-ext-host-bridge>` lookup using Squid's actual source address and ingress bridge; include any applicable policy marks. A tailnet interface in the result supports route capture, but packet marks, NAT and firewall rules can affect the actual path. No matching route or an absent table 52 alone does not rule out routing or other causes such as NET-002 and NET-006. These lookups send no traffic; redact routing details before sharing.

action: Before the AWF step, if policy permits, disable acceptance of advertised subnet routes with `tailscale set --accept-routes=false`, preserving other Tailscale preferences. Direct tailnet peer connectivity for private MCP servers was reported to keep working. Deployments requiring subnet routes or exit-node egress must use a policy-approved alternative; consult the network administrator about routes covering affected resolver and API destinations or an approved isolated runner. Do not reset unrelated Tailscale settings or bypass a required exit node. Keep the domain allowlist and DNS filtering unchanged, do not switch to a wildcard allowlist, and do not run AWF with extra host network capabilities to rewrite host routes. Report persistent HIER_NONE with redacted routing output instead of widening egress.
